facts.fact: The Civil Registration Services' questionnaire answer of December 2018 is that some local registration offices capture birth and death records electronically, in the Civil Registration and Vital Statistics System (CRVSS) then being rolled out.
facts.system: Civil Registration and Vital Statistics System (CRVSS)

facts.fact: The snapshot describes the CRVSS as a web-based electronic system automating civil registration, started by the Civil Registration Services and piloted in a number of counties (questionnaire of December 2018).
facts.system: Civil Registration and Vital Statistics System (CRVSS)

facts.fact: While the country-wide rollout of the CRVSS proceeds, CDs and flash discs are used to transmit civil registration information from sub-counties to Civil Registration Services headquarters (questionnaire of December 2018).
facts.system: Civil Registration and Vital Statistics System (CRVSS)

facts.fact: Births and deaths are registered on paper forms B1, D1 and D2 completed in duplicate under one serial number, the original kept at the local civil registration office and the duplicate sent to the Civil Registration Services in batches of 250 (questionnaire of December 2018).
facts.system: Civil Registration and Vital Statistics System (CRVSS)

facts.fact: The CRVSS has been piloted in a number of counties, the number not given, and the Civil Registration Services say scaling it to the whole country will take some time because of the resources needed (questionnaire of December 2018).
facts.system: Civil Registration and Vital Statistics System (CRVSS)

facts.fact: The Civil Registration Services answer that 'some' local registration offices capture births and deaths electronically, with no count of offices and no total given (questionnaire of December 2018).
facts.system: Civil Registration and Vital Statistics System (CRVSS)

facts.fact: The Civil Registration Services, the civil registration agency under the Ministry of Interior and Coordination of National Government, is itself modernising its information system and has started the CRVSS (questionnaire of December 2018).
facts.system: Civil Registration and Vital Statistics System (CRVSS)

facts.fact: A five-year costed strategic plan for 2018-2022, prepared in 2017 and costed at USD 62.8 million, lists the upgrade and rollout of the CRVS System among its high priorities, at an estimated USD 700,000 on the Civil Registration Services' figures.
facts.system: Civil Registration and Vital Statistics System (CRVSS)

facts.fact: The government treasury allocated USD 9.35 million to the civil registration system for July 2018 to June 2019; the expected government allocation for the CRVSS upgrade and rollout itself is given as not available, and no development partner had committed to fill the budget gap.
facts.system: Civil Registration and Vital Statistics System (CRVSS)

facts.fact: The Civil Registration Services list UNICEF as supporting comprehensive automation of CRVS business processes and Plan International as supporting CRS automation, with no amounts (questionnaire of December 2018).
facts.system: Civil Registration and Vital Statistics System (CRVSS)
